r0.why: Gas mixture called air, multi-layered, held by gravity [1]; five named layers by temperature and composition [16]; composition/temperature/pressure vary with altitude [17]; troposphere air for photosynthesis and respiration [18].

r1.why: Mass 5.15e18 kg with three-quarters within 11 km [13]; thins with altitude, no definite boundary [14]; Karman line 100 km conventional edge [15].

r2.why: Dry-air percentages by mole fraction [5]; water vapour 1% at sea level, 0.4% overall [6]; turbulent mixing to ~100 km [35]; 80-120 km transition to diffusion [36] forming heterosphere with lighter gases rising in share [37].

r3.why: Outermost, some count it interplanetary [38]; starts at thermopause/exobase atop thermosphere [39]; 500 to 1,000 km with higher solar radiation [40]; 10,000 or 190,000 km, gravity ~ radiation pressure [41,42]; geocorona of neutral hydrogen to 100,000 km [43]; mostly low-density hydrogen [44]; hundreds of km without colliding [45].

r4.why: Shields from most meteoroids and UV [3]; reduces day-night temperature variation, greenhouse warming, convective heat/moisture redistribution, conditions for life [4].
